title: The agent-model-cap role table is the one home for each role's and round's model and effort, and every reader reads it
why: Owner 15:44 CST Nov 10 (R8, M1 a, relayed by the retrospective session): "on #1 -- A seems best".
note: Ruling R33 (owner 11:09 CST Nov 11, plan ebf999a, item 3.7): every role has a chosen model and effort with a one-line reason. Rows no ruling chose today: main session, coordinator, triage, batch runner, general-purpose agents, every skill. Then an evaluation runs each role on the cheapest model that passes its checks, from measured outcomes per role and model (review pass rates, fix rounds, third tries, cost from R32's audit). A row moves only on a measured pass rate; above Sonnet needs the owner's grant. Runs after the R32 audit (step token-spend-sources). Home: decision agent-model-cap. One lane with step c201's left part (item 59 a, owner Oct 28 17:50 CDT; docs/todo.md line 9): one lane per role on one model step down, same brief shape, compared with the Measured part of agent-model-cap. The spawn guard requires the row's model and effort or fills them in (today it only permits them: guard.py:3783-3788; a no-model spawn runs reviewer.md's Haiku pin, so 17 sessions name a Haiku fix check). The merge tool checks the model that ran, not the record text. Agent frontmatter, brief markers, report_guard, check_agent_models and call_judge read the table. Each later model ruling lands in one lane that changes the table and every reader. Measured lag today 12-57 h (retrospective audit). Overlaps open lane agent-served-model-check (#2442, #2486). Home: decision agent-model-cap.
